questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Principal Normal Given Some Information About a Curve
questions.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=1$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(1)=-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k,\,{q}^{′}(1)=j+k.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2})\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{4t}{({t}^{2}+2)^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{{t}^{2}+2}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(1) & =-\frac{4(1)}{({1}^{2}+2)^{2}}\cdot q(1)+\frac{2}{{1}^{2}+2}\cdot {q}^{′}(1) \\  & =-\frac{4}{9}(-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k)+\frac{2}{3}(j+k) \\  & =\frac{4}{9}\,i+\frac{2}{9}\,j+\frac{4}{9}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(1)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{4}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{2}{9})}^{2}+{(\frac{4}{9})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{81}+\frac{4}{81}+\frac{16}{81}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{36}{81}} \\  & =\frac{6}{9} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(1)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(1) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(1)}{‖{T}^{′}(1)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{4}{9}\,i+\frac{2}{9}\,j+\frac{4}{9}\,k}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\cdot N(1) & =\frac{2}{3}q(1)\cdot (\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-i+j+\frac{1}{2}k)\cdot (\frac{2}{3}\,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j+\frac{2}{3}\,k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-\frac{2}{3}\,i\cdot \,i+\frac{1}{3}\,j\cdot j+\frac{1}{3}\,k\cdot k) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(-\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Principal Normal Given Some Information About a Curve
questions.problem:
The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot q(t).
$$

Find the principal normal vector at the point where $t=0,$ if 

$$
\begin{aligned}q(0)=⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩,\,{q}^{′}(0)=⟨1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot q(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{4+t})\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(q(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2}{{(4+t)}^{2}}\cdot q(t)+\frac{2}{4+t}\cdot {q}^{′}(t) \\  \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2}{{(4+0)}^{2}}\cdot q(0)+\frac{2}{4+0}\cdot {q}^{′}(0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{8}⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩+\frac{1}{2}⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{8}(-⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩+4⟨1,0⟩) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}⟨3,-\sqrt{3}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{1}{8}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-\sqrt{3})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{8} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(0)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve at the point where $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{1}{8}⟨3,-\sqrt{3}⟩}{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4})} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that when we find the scalar product of $T$ and $N$ at the point where $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0)\cdot N(0) & =\frac{1}{2}q(0)\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨1,\sqrt{3}⟩\cdot \frac{1}{2}⟨\sqrt{3},-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(1\cdot \sqrt{3}+\sqrt{3}\cdot (-1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{3}) \\  & =0.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Principal Normal at an Arbitrary Point
questions.problem:
$$
T(t)=\frac{1}{5}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+3\,k).
$$

The unit tangent vector to a curve at an arbitrary point is given above. Find the principal normal vector to that curve at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=$
{{field-1}}
$i\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{5}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j+3\,k)) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(-4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+4\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)\,k) \\  & =-\frac{4}{5}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we find the magnitude of ${T}^{′}(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\frac{4}{5}‖\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j‖ \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{4}{5}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)}{\frac{4}{5}} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=⟨4\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3t,\,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$, find the principal normal vector $N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=⟨$
{{field-1}}
$,\,0\,,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3,\,-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(3)^{2}+(-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+9} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,3,\,-4\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\frac{3}{5},\,-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{3}{5}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  & =\frac{4}{5}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\  \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{(\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{25}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{4}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{\frac{4}{5}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩}{(\frac{4}{5})} \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the curve $r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,4t⟩$, find the principal normal vector $N(t)$ at an arbitrary point on the curve.

$N(t)=⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,$
{{field-1}}$,0\,⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the unit tangent vector $T(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)+16} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{4}{5}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal $N(t).$ To do this, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{3}{5}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(-\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(\frac{3}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{9}{25}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${T}^{′}(t)$ and obtain the principal normal to the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}N(t) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(t)}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{\frac{3}{5}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩}{(\frac{3}{5})}=⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$
